rationale: bugs_open/309: fundamentallyai.com's Platform Log index serves six complete-looking article cards with ZERO anchors. Root cause, verified first-hand at live DB + code: the generated component blog-listing_pre_037 declares its six required post URLs as source site_specs.blog.postN_url — and NO site in fleet history has ever carried a site_specs aspect named 'blog' (SELECT ... WHERE aspect='blog' → 0 rows, all history). plan_sections resolves nothing, on_missing defaults to skip_field even for required fields, and the template's {{if .postN_url}} gates silently drop every anchor. This is a CLASS, not a case: censused 2026-08-18, 11 active components declare 10 site_specs aspects that exist on no site (58 fields; nav alone has 16), 7 query.* names in active schemas are unknown to queryresolve.Resolve's switch (each errors at plan time and skip_fields silently), and 3 fields carry prefixes outside the vocabulary entirely. The store gate (store_generated_component_action.go) validates template structure, truncation, and schema dialect — it has NEVER validated that a declared source is resolvable. The fix is a birth gate: (1) refactor queryresolve's dispatch switch into a single handler map and export IsKnownQueryName/KnownQueryBases from it, so the dispatcher and the validator answer from ONE structure and cannot drift; (2) a new component_source_guard.go whose pure sourceVocabularyIssues() flags unknown prefixes, unregistered query names, and site_specs aspects absent from the live aspect vocabulary (loaded per store; a failed load skips ONLY the aspect half, fail-open, so a transient DB error cannot block all component generation); (3) wire it into the existing Layer-1 blockingIssues sequence, feeding the existing recordValidationRejection channel so refusals are queryable and the component-creator gets an instructive retry message naming the real vocabulary. Calibration per house style (the fabricated-fallback guard's precedent): against every active component's schema the guard flags ONLY the 58+7+3 fields above, every one of which currently resolves nowhere — zero refusals of anything that works today. Known consequence, stated: a REGENERATION of one of the 11 phantom-source components must repoint its sources or be repaired by migration (the stranded-fields check keeps the field names, this guard refuses their sources) — deliberate, same shape as the fabricated-fallback guard's regeneration note. Consumer notified: component-creator is the sole producer through this gate; its failure path already handles pre-store rejection messages. The 309 case itself is repaired separately by swapping the page's section to the framework-native content-listing (query.blog_posts) and rebuilding — no hand-patched HTML, no content_data surgery. An independent 090 diagnosis with the same symptom (corr df8ca3a1-9cca-474a-88fb-19577e088080, fired by the filing thread) is queued and will be read as cross-check when it lands.

plan.summary: A generated component can declare data sources the platform cannot resolve — a phantom site_specs aspect, an unregistered query name, an unknown prefix — and nothing between generation and render checks; the value silently skip_fields and pages ship complete-looking but data-less markup (bugs_open/309: an article index whose every card is link-less). This change adds source-vocabulary validation to the existing pre-store Layer-1 gate in store_generated_component_action.go, backed by a queryresolve refactor that makes the query vocabulary a single answerable structure.

edits.rationale: The query.* vocabulary lived only as a switch statement, so nothing else could ask 'would this name resolve?' — which is how 7 phantom query names entered component schemas unnoticed. Convert the switch to a package-level map[string]queryHandler that Resolve dispatches through, and export IsKnownQueryName(name) + KnownQueryBases() answered from the same map. Behaviour-preserving: every case's handler call and comment carried over verbatim; unknown names return the same error string.

The birth gate for declared sources. Pure half sourceVocabularyIssues(schemaJSON, knownSpecAspects) returns one issue per field whose source cannot resolve for ANY site: unknown prefix (outside llm/renderer/static/site_specs/site_assets/pages/config/query), unregistered query.* name (via queryresolve.IsKnownQueryName), or site_specs.<aspect> where the aspect appears in no site_specs row in fleet history. DB half loadKnownSpecAspects reads SELECT DISTINCT aspect FROM site_specs (superseded rows deliberately included — an aspect with only historical rows still names a store a writer produces). nil aspect set = loader failed = aspect half SKIPPED (fail open), prefix/query halves still run. Leaf-level site_specs/site_assets/pages paths deliberately NOT checked: those are per-site facts resolved at plan time; only the fleet-wide vocabulary is checkable at birth without over-firing.
edits.sketch:
func sourceVocabularyIssues(inputSchemaJSON string, knownSpecAspects map[string]bool) []string { // walk fields sorted; bare {"",llm,renderer,static} pass; strings.Cut on '.'; unknown prefix -> issue; query -> !IsKnownQueryName -> issue naming KnownQueryBases(); site_specs -> aspect not in set -> issue naming real aspects + 'for listing data use a query.* source' }
func loadKnownSpecAspects(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB) (map[string]bool, error) { rows, err := db.QueryContext(ctx, `SELECT DISTINCT aspect FROM site_specs`); ... }

plan.risks: 1) Over-refusal: the guard could block legitimate generations. Mitigated by calibration — against every active component's schema it flags only fields that currently resolve nowhere (58 phantom-aspect + 7 unknown-query + 3 unknown-prefix), zero flags on anything that works; and the aspect half fails OPEN on a DB read error. A reviewer should check the calibration claim's construction: the flagged set was derived by the same census queries the guard's predicate encodes, so the zero-false-positive claim is true by construction against TODAY's corpus — a component whose aspect is created tomorrow passes tomorrow (the set is read live per store). 2) Regeneration trap: the 11 existing phantom-source components cannot re-store their schemas unchanged; the stranded-fields check forces keeping field NAMES while this guard refuses their SOURCES — a regeneration must repoint sources or the component needs a migration. Deliberate (fabricated-fallback precedent) but a reviewer should confirm no automated regeneration loop currently targets those 11 (the census found 5 with zero live usage rows and none in open regeneration work items — worth re-checking at review time). 3) The queryresolve switch→map conversion must be behaviour-preserving; a reviewer should diff each map entry's handler call against the old switch arm (25 cases, mechanical). 4) The store-action wiring commit is deliberately HELD until another session's uncommitted symbol (content.UnbalancedStructuralTags) lands at HEAD — until then the guard exists but is not called; the 098 report will show the wiring commit following the others. 5) No wiring-level test asserts the guard is called from StoreGeneratedComponentAction (unit tests call the pure function directly); a mutation deleting the wiring line would pass the suite. Accepted for now and stated here rather than hidden.
